searchText: hey guys, which clients pass all pyspec tests, (specially EOFCREATE AND RETURNCONTRACT tests)? In context of EOF, evmone passes all. Besu passes too. if you use the main branch. Geth currently fails a few EOFCREATE tests and one RJUMP test, but is passing all other merged tests. If you use marius's mega-eof branch. EthJS passes all too That is, this one https://github.com/ethereum/execution-spec-tests/releases/tag/eip7692%40v1.0.5 Not sure if those are the pyspec tests erc-5202, not general data contract standard, but some kind of factory contract standard Thanks, this is handy. <@508125616940515329> <@1011612262743679036> <@429719902363058177> do you have a CLI or script that can run arbitrary state or block test JSONs? Or do these need to be loaded into your client build to execute? There is binary to run statetests. Install rust, download revm repo, and use `cargo run --release -p revme statetest tests/eof_suite/state_tests/`. Executable if needed can be found at `~/target/release/revme` We can run them directly from our VM 🙂 Let me find the instructions Ah! I posted the instructions on how to run the fixtures in the Mega EOF PR: https://github.com/ethereumjs/ethereumjs-monorepo/pull/3440 It shows how to run the state/blockchain and eof header validation tests 🙂 If you need help integrating it into something let me know, happy to assist 🙂 Is this being discussed elsewhere? https://mariusvanderwijden.github.io/blog/2024/07/12/EOF/ The part I care about, <@360491619402776577> is > As long as the EVM contains non-static jumps, the analysis of a program is in the worst case O(n^2). EOF removes dynamic jumps which reduces the analysis to O(n) in the worst case. > > I’m not convinced that that the difference is significant though, since EVM programs are inherently small in size. Even at the worst case of 24576 byte, the analysis needs ~600 million steps. Assuming 1000ns per step (which is quite a lot, for reference KECCAK takes <700ns on my machine) this can be analysis be done in 10 minutes. But others have been convinced since 2016 that this is a problem. EWasm was abandoned in part because JITing fuzzed codes could sometimes take seconds rather milliseconds.
